title: Robot Car Chase Arena
description: The player controls an Xbot robot navigating a flat arena while a concept car patrols autonomously. The robot must reach 5 glowing checkpoint orbs scattered around the arena without being caught by the car, which accelerates and pursues the player when they get close. A HUD displays checkpoints collected, distance to nearest checkpoint, and a stamina bar for sprinting.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a robot-vs-car chase game. Load CarConcept.glb and Xbot.glb using GLTFLoader. Place both models on a large flat ground plane (80x80 units, dark grid-textured using MeshStandardMaterial with a repeating grid pattern). The Xbot starts at the center; the CarConcept starts at a random edge. Generate 5 glowing checkpoint spheres (emissive yellow, radius 0.5) at random positions on the arena. Camera: third-person follow camera that smoothly tracks behind the Xbot at an offset of (0, 8, -12), using lerp for smooth transitions. Lighting: one DirectionalLight casting shadows, one HemisphereLight for ambient fill, and PointLights on each checkpoint orb. Player controls: WASD moves the Xbot with rotation facing movement direction. Shift key activates sprint (1.8x speed) which drains a stamina bar over 3 seconds and regenerates when not sprinting. Play the Xbot walk animation from its embedded AnimationClip when moving, idle when stopped, and blend to run animation during sprint. The CarConcept patrols in a rectangular path by default. When the Xbot is within 20 units, the car switches to pursuit mode: it rotates toward the Xbot and accelerates to 1.5x the Xbot normal speed. If the car reaches within 1.5 units of the Xbot, display a red CAUGHT overlay, reset the robot to center, and deduct one collected checkpoint. When the Xbot reaches within 1.2 units of a checkpoint, collect it with a particle burst effect (20 small spheres expanding outward then fading). HUD overlay using HTML/CSS: show checkpoints collected out of 5, a stamina bar, and distance to nearest checkpoint. When all 5 checkpoints are collected, display a victory screen with elapsed time and a Restart button. Ensure all models are scaled appropriately so the robot is roughly human-sized and the car is proportionally larger. Add fog to the scene for atmosphere.
